nodes.name: app.py
nodes.summary: Hosts the Flask dashboard that coordinates dataset-backed patient selection, model prediction, SHAP explanations, what-if simulation, current and scenario SMPL twins, and the temporary Stage 4 graph.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses lazy singleton loading for the large model and server-side validation for numbered patient rows and uploaded CSV datasets.

nodes.name: PatientDataset
nodes.summary: Validates an active BRFSS patient table, enforces feature ranges, and exposes stable one-based patient lookup, labels, and nearby-row summaries for the dashboard.

nodes.name: get_patient_dataset
nodes.summary: Lazily loads and caches the default BRFSS dataset as the dashboard's active numbered patient source.

nodes.name: get_twin
nodes.summary: Lazily constructs and caches the model-backed Digital Twin when prediction is first requested.

nodes.name: twin_metadata
nodes.summary: Reads optional metadata beside a GLB twin and adds a modification-time version token, with resilient fallbacks for missing or malformed metadata.

nodes.name: digital_twin_asset
nodes.summary: Serves the current-patient GLB Digital Twin through a conditional Flask response or returns 404 when unavailable.

nodes.name: scenario_digital_twin_asset
nodes.summary: Serves the independently generated scenario-profile GLB Digital Twin through the dashboard.

nodes.name: refresh_smpl_twin
nodes.summary: Regenerates a patient-specific SMPL GLB from BMI, sex, and modeled risk, reusing matching output and falling back from direct Python export to Docker Compose.

nodes.name: index
nodes.summary: Handles dashboard GET and POST flows for importing patient data, selecting a numbered patient, predicting or simulating risk, generating twins, and assembling all template results.

nodes.name: knowledge_graph.py
nodes.summary: Implements the Stage 4 patient-centric knowledge graph: Neo4j persists only reusable definitions and model metadata, while complete patient observations, probabilities, SHAP contributions, and twin nodes are assembled in memory.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses idempotent Cypher constraints and a lock-protected lazy initializer, with a local attribute fallback when Neo4j is unavailable.

nodes.name: classify_bmi
nodes.summary: Maps a nonnegative BMI value to the prototype's ordered adult BMI category definitions.

nodes.name: _integer_code
nodes.summary: Converts a numeric categorical value to an integer and rejects non-whole codes.

nodes.name: decode_feature
nodes.summary: Decodes BRFSS feature values into dataset-grounded patient-readable states without adding clinical severity or causal interpretation.

nodes.name: _format_value
nodes.summary: Formats numeric feature values compactly while preserving fractional values when present.

nodes.name: _safe_id
nodes.summary: Normalizes display strings into lowercase hyphenated identifiers for temporary graph elements.

nodes.name: PatientKnowledgeGraph
nodes.summary: Lazily initializes reusable Neo4j schema and model evaluation nodes, then joins them with live profile and model outputs to return a Cytoscape-ready graph without persisting patient data.

nodes.name: stage3.py
nodes.summary: Provides the Stage 3 model-backed Digital Twin for three-class prediction, version-tolerant SHAP explanation, manual what-if comparison, and SMPL visual descriptors.
nodes.languageNotes: Normalizes multiple SHAP array layouts and treats simulation as a non-causal comparison of model estimates.

nodes.name: find_model_path
nodes.summary: Selects the first available trained model artifact from the configured candidate paths and reports all searched locations when none exists.

nodes.name: DiabetesDigitalTwin
nodes.summary: Wraps the trained risk model to validate profiles, predict class probabilities, rank patient-level SHAP factors, and compare baseline with manually edited scenarios.

nodes.name: smpl_twin_descriptor
nodes.summary: Derives a lightweight SMPL descriptor from BMI and high-risk probability, including body-shape coefficient, risk color band, and licensed-weight availability.

nodes.name: test_knowledge_graph.py
nodes.summary: Tests the Stage 4 graph schema, decoding boundaries, temporary patient model completeness, SHAP and probability fidelity, idempotent initialization, and Neo4j-unavailable fallback behavior.

nodes.name: FakeResult
nodes.summary: Minimal iterable Neo4j result double that supports consumption in initialization tests.

nodes.name: FakeSession
nodes.summary: Context-managed Neo4j session double that records Cypher calls and returns reusable attribute definitions for graph assembly tests.

nodes.name: FakeDriver
nodes.summary: Neo4j driver double that exposes one inspectable fake session to the graph service.

nodes.name: example_profile
nodes.summary: Builds a complete 21-feature example profile with representative BMI and categorical values.

nodes.name: example_prediction
nodes.summary: Provides a deterministic high-risk prediction fixture with all three class probabilities.

nodes.name: example_contributions
nodes.summary: Builds one SHAP contribution fixture for each of the 21 model features, including positive, negative, and neutral examples.

nodes.name: explain
nodes.summary: Invokes the graph service with the standard profile, prediction, SHAP, twin, and model fixtures.

nodes.name: KnowledgeGraphTests
nodes.summary: Verifies feature coverage, category decoding, complete temporary graph composition, non-causal semantics, model evidence, idempotency, and disconnected fallback behavior.

nodes.name: diabetes_risk.py
nodes.summary: Defines the shared BRFSS feature schema, risk labels, artifact paths, and validation, serialization, and model-loading helpers used throughout Stages 1-4.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typed path unions and pandas schema checks to keep training and patient inference inputs aligned.

nodes.name: load_dataset
nodes.summary: Loads a BRFSS CSV, enforces the 21-feature plus target schema, removes incomplete rows, and returns features with a validated three-class target.

nodes.name: validate_patient
nodes.summary: Validates that a patient frame contains exactly one complete row with the expected BRFSS features and returns it in model order as floats.

nodes.name: save_json
nodes.summary: Serializes artifact dictionaries as indented JSON while converting NumPy scalar values to native Python types.

nodes.name: load_model
nodes.summary: Loads the persisted diabetes-risk estimator from the configured joblib artifact path.

nodes.name: explain_patient.py
nodes.summary: Implements the Stage 2 command-line workflow for validating one patient, predicting risk, calculating class-specific SHAP contributions, and saving JSON, CSV, and waterfall-plot artifacts.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles both list-per-class and three-dimensional SHAP output conventions for tree models.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Defines command-line options for a patient CSV, model artifact, or example patient template.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs single-patient inference and SHAP explanation, writes ranked contributions and a waterfall visualization, and reports the predicted risk probabilities.

nodes.name: train.py
nodes.summary: Implements Stage 1 training and evaluation for a class-balanced three-class Random Forest, producing the model, metrics, confusion matrix, ROC curves, and held-out permutation importance artifacts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses stratified splitting, balanced subsample weights, macro metrics, and held-out permutation importance to account for class imbalance.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Defines training CLI options for the BRFSS dataset, split size, random seed, and forest size.

nodes.name: save_roc_curve
nodes.summary: Builds and saves one-vs-rest ROC curves with per-class AUC labels for the three risk categories.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Trains the balanced Random Forest on a stratified split, evaluates overall and per-class performance, and persists model and diagnostic artifacts.

nodes.name: .dockerignore
nodes.summary: Defines the Docker build-context exclusions for local environments, generated artifacts, archived files, licensed SMPL weights, trained models, and execution logs.

nodes.name: Dockerfile
nodes.summary: Builds the shared Python 3.11 CPU image used for the Flask dashboard, Jupyter training, and SMPL export, installing PyTorch and legacy Chumpy support before copying the project and dropping to a non-root user.
nodes.languageNotes: The dependency-first copy order preserves Docker layer caching, while CPU-only PyTorch and NumPy 1.x compatibility support reproducible local execution.

nodes.name: python
nodes.summary: Represents the Python 3.11 slim container stage that installs project dependencies, exposes Flask and Jupyter ports, and defaults to running the dashboard.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Orchestrates Neo4j, the Flask dashboard, JupyterLab, notebook execution, and optional SMPL mesh export from one shared project image, with localhost-only ports and persistent Neo4j storage.
nodes.languageNotes: Compose profiles isolate one-shot training and SMPL export jobs from the default dashboard workflow.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Provides local Neo4j username, password, and Bolt URI defaults for the Docker Compose deployment without embedding patient data.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Introduces the four-stage explainable diabetes-risk Digital Twin, documents local and Docker workflows, and defines the model-derived, non-causal research boundary for prediction, SHAP, simulation, Neo4j, and SMPL outputs.

nodes.name: SMPL_SETUP.md
nodes.summary: Explains the optional Stage 3 SMPL pathway, licensed model asset placement, BMI and risk mappings, Docker export commands, and the dashboard's patient-specific GLB workflow.

nodes.name: SUPERVISOR_HANDOFF.md
nodes.summary: Defines a safe supervisor-sharing package, a concise demonstration sequence, an evidence-oriented status table, and limitations concerning BRFSS data, minority-class performance, and non-causal simulation.

nodes.name: SYSTEM_USER_GUIDE.md
nodes.summary: Guides users through starting the Docker dashboard, selecting or importing numbered patients, interpreting Stages 1-4, comparing scenarios, and diagnosing basic container failures.

nodes.name: WEBSITE_REVIEW.md
nodes.summary: Reviews the dataset-linked dashboard against supervisor feedback and research-stage expectations, recording patient consistency checks alongside BRFSS, causal, and SMPL calibration gaps.

nodes.name: plan.md
nodes.summary: Lays out the original Stage 3 implementation plan for mapping BMI and model risk into an SMPL body shape and colour, exporting a mesh, and integrating the result with a web what-if workflow.

nodes.name: requirements.txt
nodes.summary: Pins and constrains the Python dependencies for model training, imbalance handling, SHAP explanation, Flask and Neo4j integration, Jupyter, and SMPL mesh generation.
nodes.languageNotes: NumPy remains below version 2 and scikit-learn is pinned to preserve compatibility with checked-in CPU PyTorch and model artifacts.

nodes.name: research-question-card.md
nodes.summary: Frames the applied research question around consistent reuse of one numbered dataset record across prediction, SHAP explanation, 3D representation, and manual what-if simulation, with explicit supporting and falsifying evidence.

nodes.name: share_supervisor.ps1
nodes.summary: Builds a timestamped supervisor ZIP containing source, documentation, notebook, and small evidence artifacts while excluding raw data, trained models, virtual environments, bytecode, and licensed SMPL weights.
nodes.languageNotes: The script stages an allowlisted package, recursively filters source folders, and removes the temporary staging directory after compression.

nodes.name: diabetes_risk_stages_1_2.ipynb
nodes.summary: Research notebook implementing the reproducible Stages 1-3 workflow: three-class diabetes-risk training and evaluation, global and patient-level explanations, and a dataset-linked manual Digital Twin scenario. It records class-imbalance-aware metrics and explicitly frames SHAP and scenario changes as non-causal research evidence.
nodes.languageNotes: The notebook combines executable Python cells with methodology notes, held-out evaluation, SHAP analysis, and a patient-linked simulation in one shareable artifact.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Documents where licensed female or male SMPL model files must be placed and names the exact legacy model filenames expected by the twin generator.

nodes.name: export_smpl.py
nodes.summary: Command-line exporter that generates a patient-shaped SMPL mesh from BMI and sex, colors it from model risk, writes GLB or OBJ output, and saves matching JSON metadata without requiring PyVista.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses BMI, risk, gender, and output arguments, generates and colors the SMPL mesh, then exports the mesh and its patient-specific metadata.

nodes.name: twin_generator.py
nodes.summary: Provides the SMPL patient Digital Twin engine, including BMI-to-shape mapping, risk-color encoding, lazy loading of licensed legacy model weights, mesh generation, and an optional PyVista viewer.
nodes.languageNotes: The loader adds targeted Python 3.11 and NumPy compatibility aliases for legacy Chumpy-based SMPL pickle files, while PyVista remains lazily imported for headless export support.

nodes.name: bmi_to_beta0
nodes.summary: Maps patient BMI to the first SMPL shape coefficient using the project's fixed linear research mapping.

nodes.name: risk_to_color
nodes.summary: Converts a risk percentage into green, orange, or red presentation colors using explicit threshold bands.

nodes.name: TwinGenerator
nodes.summary: Loads and caches the sex-specific licensed SMPL model, runs CPU mesh generation from patient BMI, and optionally wraps the result as a risk-colored PyVista mesh.

nodes.name: display_demo
nodes.summary: Generates a sample risk-colored patient mesh and displays it interactively in a PyVista window for local inspection.

nodes.name: knowledge_graph.js
nodes.summary: Initializes the patient-centric Cytoscape knowledge graph, styles clinical-observation and model-evidence node groups, and supports node inspection, filtering, reset, responsive relayout, and accessible fallback behavior.
nodes.languageNotes: A browser-scoped IIFE keeps graph state private while exposing only the initialized Cytoscape instance for inspection.

nodes.name: style.css
nodes.summary: Defines the responsive visual system for patient selection, risk results, SHAP factors, Stage 4 graph inspection, and current-versus-scenario 3D twin comparison cards.
nodes.languageNotes: CSS custom properties centralize the research dashboard palette, with grid breakpoints adapting the graph and twin comparison layouts for narrow screens.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Primary Flask/Jinja dashboard template joining patient import and selection with Stages 1-4 outputs: probabilities, SHAP evidence, an interactive knowledge graph, current SMPL twin, and manual scenario comparison.
nodes.languageNotes: Jinja conditionals progressively render available model, graph, and mesh results, while model-viewer scripts recolor each current or scenario GLB from its own risk metadata.

layers.name: Application Entry and API Layer
layers.description: Exposes the Flask dashboard and command-line entry points for patient explanation and SMPL mesh export workflows.

layers.name: Digital Twin Service Layer
layers.description: Implements Stage 3 simulation, Stage 4 explain-only graph assembly, and patient-specific SMPL twin generation.

layers.name: Data and Machine Learning Layer
layers.description: Defines the shared BRFSS schema and model helpers and runs reproducible training, evaluation, SHAP, and scenario research pipelines.

layers.name: Browser UI Layer
layers.description: Renders the Jinja dashboard and supplies responsive styling and interactive Cytoscape behavior for Stages 1-4.

layers.name: Validation and Test Layer
layers.description: Verifies Stage 4 graph completeness, patient-data boundaries, model evidence fidelity, idempotence, and Neo4j fallback behavior.

layers.name: Infrastructure and Configuration
layers.description: Packages and orchestrates Flask, Jupyter, Neo4j, and SMPL workflows while defining dependencies, local settings, privacy exclusions, and supervisor handoff automation.

layers.name: Research and User Documentation
layers.description: Documents setup, operation, SMPL assets, research framing, validation evidence, limitations, and safe project handoff.
